name: SikaGrout GP AU
paste:
SIKAGROUT® GP AU: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaGrout® GP AU, July 2025, Version 01.05 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/i/sikagrout-gp-au.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaGrout® GP AU where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2025, Version 01.05).
1.2 Product description. SikaGrout® GP AU is a pumpable, shrinkage-compensated, flowable cementitious "Class A" grout with extended working time to suit local ambient temperatures.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. SikaGrout® GP AU is a general purpose grout suitable for the following applications:
    - General purpose grouting
    - Grouting works for machine foundations, anchor bolts etc.
    - Precast grouting
    - Filling of cavities, gaps, recesses, etc.
    For precision grouting, SikaGrout®-212HP is recommended.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaGrout® GP AU
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: GENERAL PURPOSE, "CLASS A" PUMPABLE, SHRINKAGE-COMPENSATED CEMENTITIOUS GROUT
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Certificates and test reports. Department of Main Roads Qld (TMR) 2019, Product Index for Bridges and Other Structures, Section 5. Registered and Conforming Products, 5.33 Repair Materials (Concrete) – Grouts
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS 1478.2:2005: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.1).
    - AS 1478.2-2005: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Expansion (p.2).
    - AS 2350.4:2006: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Setting time (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - ▪ Easy to mix and apply
    - ▪ Flowable consistency (according to mix)
    - ▪ Rapid strength development
    - ▪ Non-corrosive
    - ▪ Non-toxic
    - ▪ Iron and chloride free
    - ▪ Shrinkage-compensated
    - ▪ Good pumping properties
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Appearance and colour: Grey premixed powder
    - Density: ~ 2.2 kg/l (depending on consistency and temperature)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Maximum grain size: Dmax: 0.4 mm
    - Expansion: max 3.0 % (Flowable consistency ) (AS 1478.2-2005)
2.7 Compressive strength.
    | Stiff | Plastic | Flowable |
    | 1 day | ~ 25 MPa | ~ 20 MPa | ~ 12 MPa |
    | 7days | ~ 50 MPa | ~ 45 MPa | ~ 35 MPa |
    | 28 days | ~ 60 MPa | ~ 55 MPa | ~ 50 MPa |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (AS 1478.2:2005)
    Note printed: Material and curing conditions at 23°C / 50% r.h. The results are based on 50mm x 50mm cube specimens.
2.8 Electrical resistivity.
    | 7 days | ~ 4,000 Ω.cm |
    | 28 days | ~ 4,500 Ω.cm |
    | 56 days | ~ 4,600 Ω.cm |
    | 90 days | ~ 5,000 Ω.cm |
    Test method printed: (FM5-578)
    Note printed: 50mm Probe Spacing
2.9 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 20 kg bag
    - Shelf life: 9 months from the date of production
    - Storage conditions: Store properly in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +10 °C and +35 °C. Protect from direct sunlight.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2025, Version 01.05) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment.
    - The substrate should be prepared by suitable mechanical preparation techniques such as high pressure water, breakers, grit blasting, scabblers, etc. All absorbent surfaces must be well saturated with clean water, but free of any surface water or puddles prior to the application of SikaGrout® GP AU. Concrete, mortar and stone
    - Surfaces must be sound, clean, free from frost, oils, grease, standing water and all loosely adhering particles and other surface contaminants.
    - Metal surfaces (iron and steel)
    - Surfaces should be clean, free from scale, rust, oil and grease.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2025, Version 01.05) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Pot Life: 30 mins approx.
4.3 Mixing ratio. Water addition per 20 kg bag (litre/s)
    | Stiff | Plastic | Flowable |
    | 2.9 - 3.0 | 3.2 - 3.4 | 4.0 - 4.6 |
    Note printed: These mix ratios are a guide and preliminary trials at local temperatures / humidity conditions are recommended.
4.4 Consumption. Approximate number of bags per 1.0 m³
    | Stiff | Plastic | Flowable |
    | 96 | 94 | 90 |
4.5 Yield.
    | Stiff | Plastic | Flowable |
    | 10.4 litres | 10.6 litres | 11.1 litres |
4.6 Layer thickness.
    | Consistency | Thickness |
    | Stiff & Plastic | 10 mm min. / 100 mm max. |
    | Flowable | 10 mm min. / 50 mm max. |
4.7 Setting time.
    | Temperature | Initial Set | Final Set |
    | 23 °C | ~ 3 hrs | ~ 4 hrs 45 mins |
    Test method printed: (AS 2350.4:2006)
4.8 Mixing. Place about 70–80 % of the premeasured clean water (depending on consistency required – refer to “Mix Ratio”) into a clean container and gradually add the whole bag of SikaGrout® GP AU into it while continuously mixing. Add the remaining water until the desired consistency is obtained. Mix for 3–5 minutes with a low speed drill (500 rpm max.).
4.9 Application. After mixing, stir lightly with a spatula for a few seconds to release any entrapped air. The grout is then poured immediately into the prepared formwork. When carrying out baseplate grouting, ensure sufficient pressure head is maintained for uninterrupted mortar flow. For formwork repair, the prepared formwork must be firmly in place and kept watertight. When placing grout over a large area, it is important to maintain a continuous flow throughout. Work sequence must be properly organised to ensure an uninterrupted flow. In large areas, SikaGrout® GP AU may be pumped using heavy duty diaphragm pumps. Screw feed and piston pumps may also be used.
4.10 Application - Grouting under baseplate Flowable consistency.
    | Formwork grouting - pouring method | Flowable consistency |
    | Formwork grouting - prepacked method | Flowable / Plastic consistency |
    | Grouting anchor bolts | Plastic / Stiff consistency |
    | Dry packed / Precast grouting | Stiff consistency |
    Grouting large volumes: For sections thicker than 100 mm, it is necessary to fill ikaGrout® GP AU with graded 10 mm silt free aggregates o minimise temperature rise generated during the during stage. The quantity of aggregates should not exceed 1 part aggregates to 1 part SikaGrout® GP AU by weight. For such mixes, a conventional concrete mixer and pump may be used. To further ensure that air entrapped during mixing is allowed to fully escape, it may be necessary to make breather holes. Use steel rods or chains to assist the flow of grout where necessary. Preliminary trials are recommended.
4.11 Curing treatment. When formwork type repair is used, leave the formwork in place for at least 3 days. Upon removal of the formwork, cure the exposed surfaces immediately with Antisol® curing compound or use other approved curing methods.
4.12 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with water immediately after use. Hardened or cured material can only be mechanically removed.
4.13 Further documentation. SikaGrout and Sikadur products are tested in accordance with Australian Standards and/or Internationally accepted Standards. The published performance data is achieved by testing strictly in accordance to the procedures of these standards. Any test procedures performed by others on our products that are not in strict accordance with the standard in every facet will likely produce results different from the published above. On site testing by others can be affected by external factors such as incorrect mixing methods, poor sampling techniques, varying temperatures, curing, crushing procedures etc. Sika can provide Certificates of Compliance of all products delivered to site prior to installation if required. If results of site testing or testing facilities by others vary from the Sika published data we recommend the following items be reviewed before contacting the manufacturer as one or all of these items could be influencing the results attained on site. These include but are not limited to the following: site conditions, ambient, substrate and product temperature, mixing equipment, mixer speed, pump equipment, contractor experience, and incorrect test methods. Sika Australia do not take responsibility nor have to make a case for any such tests where results of testing by others do not achieve the published data as above.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +10 °C min. / +35 °C max.
5.3 Substrate temperature. +10 °C min. / +35 °C max.
5.4 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Compressive strength: Stiff | Plastic | Flowable; 1 day | ~ 25 MPa | ~ 20 MPa | ~ 12 MPa; 7days | ~ 50 MPa | ~ 45 MPa | ~ 35 MPa; 28 days | ~ 60 MPa | ~ 55 MPa | ~ 50 MPa (AS 1478.2:2005)
    - Expansion: max 3.0 % (Flowable consistency ) (AS 1478.2-2005)
    - Electrical resistivity: 7 days | ~ 4,000 Ω.cm; 28 days | ~ 4,500 Ω.cm; 56 days | ~ 4,600 Ω.cm; 90 days | ~ 5,000 Ω.cm (FM5-578)
    - Setting time: Temperature | Initial Set | Final Set; 23 °C | ~ 3 hrs | ~ 4 hrs 45 mins (AS 2350.4:2006)
5.5 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.6 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaGrout® GP AU, July 2025, Version 01.05, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/i/sikagrout-gp-au.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaGrout® GP AU, version 09/04/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/u/sds-sikagrout-gpau.pdf
    - Environmental Product Declaration: SikaGrout® GP AU EPD, version 15/04/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/m/sikagrout-gp-au-epd.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
